articles.title: How worried should Kilmarnock fans be by losing start?
articles.summary: What is going wrong at Kilmarnock amid losing start to Scottish Premiership season?
articles.body:
Three games, zero points and 13 goals conceded - the new-season optimism at Kilmarnock has quickly evaporated.

The Rugby Park side were booed off at half-time and full-time of Saturday's 4-0 mauling by Dundee United which didn't overly flatter the visitors.

Manager Neil McCann kept a lid on his anger post match, refusing to let rip despite a first-half horror show that had his side three goals down and once again chasing a Scottish Premiership match from the bottom of an unscalable cliff.

McCann was quick to acknowledge that the fury of the home support was entirely justified.

"I'm angry and I'm apologetic to the fans," he said.

"It's very easy right now to be emotional about it. The guys know my feelings about the performance and I expect a reaction on Wednesday night [against St Mirren].

"I'm not overly emotional right now. I had a wee chat to them in the dressing room. They know that they've let everybody down today and I've been a part of that.

"We've let everybody down connected with Kilmarnock but there's no better thing in sport than a quick game and we've all got an opportunity to put things right on Wednesday night."

Dundee Utd boost hospitalised Goodwin with Kilmarnock rout

As Kilmarnock seek their first point of the season, the stats paint a bleak picture for supporters. Since 1998-99, McCann's side have made the joint-worst start by a Scottish top-flight team after three games.

Aberdeen in 2000, Dundee United in 2004, Hamilton in 2010 and Kilmarnock themselves in 2025 all had no points and a goal difference of minus nine after the opening three fixtures.

As if that's not bad enough, Kilmarnock's 13 goals conceded is also the worst by any team in the same period, as well as being the most by a distance of any Premiership team this term.

McCann's men also have the highest expected goals against of 10.14 this season, as well as the most errors leading to goals (six, four more than any side in the division).

You'll not be surprised to discover they've faced the most shots (69) while also allowed the most shots on target (29).

The only be marginal consolation for McCann is his side is not last when it comes to tackles and tackles won - they're ninth for that, with 36 and 22 respectively.

McCann was something of a surprise choice to take the reins at Rugby Park in January of last season as the club floundered at the wrong end of the table.

However, alongside assistant Billy Dodds and helped by the sparkling loan impact of Rangers winger Findlay Curtis, he steered Killie to survival with a flourish. They ended last term with four straight league wins, rattling in 13 goals.

The downturn has been swift. To concede four goals to St Johnstone, five to Celtic and then another four to Dundee United means the pressure from his own supporters is mounting by the minute.

The team's expansive style is leaving them wide open.

Andy Halliday, the former Rangers, Hearts and Motherwell midfielder, says their shape is suspect.

He told BBC Sportsound: "I felt there was a lot of promise for Kilmarnock coming into this season, given that from when McCann in to the end of the season, they rose to fourth in the form table.

"I don't think they look comfortable in their shape. I hated playing in [a diamond]. When you're the wide man in that, you're asked to do a power of work, in and out of possession. Quite often, you have to be the width when on the ball and then narrow when you're out of possession.

"The worry for me when I watch Kilmarnock is the way the full-backs operate. They're asked to do a really attacking job in possession, but out of possession they're one-v-one.

"They don't have Findlay Curtis or the like in front of them, with high energy, who can come back and double up. As much as they're struggling defensively, I don't think the shape is helping because they're exposed."

It's not that Kilmarnock didn't have chances against United, it's just that they couldn't take them. That said, at the other end, Max Stryjek was beaten four times yet could still say he had a pretty decent game.

Debuts handed to centre-half Cathal McCarthy and Jonathan Meier meant half the defence were getting their first taste of the Premiership. Too much too soon?

McCarthy gave away the penalty and Meier was hooked at half-time. An early injury to centre-half stalwart Robbie Deas added to Kilmarnock's woe.

Everything that could go wrong, did. Does St Mirren's visit on Wednesday already fall into the 'must win' category? It certainly feels like a 'must not lose' if Killie are to kickstart their season.

articles.title: Irish Premiership: In-form quartet all win to snap at the heels of leaders Coleraine - story of the day
articles.summary: BBC Sport NI explores the main talking point of the weekend from within the Irish Premiership.
articles.body:
Who says it is too early to look at the Irish Premiership table?

It is, off course, too soon to be talking about title races, European places and relegation battles but there has been plenty to ponder after week four of the Irish Premiership which yielded a clean sweep of five away wins.

Currently, four teams sit on nine points after winning three games and losing one, the in-form quartet tucked in just one point behind early leaders Coleraine.

Dungannon Swifts, Carrick Rangers, Crusaders and Linfield all won their fixtures on Saturday to occupy second to fifth and have impressed so far.

But what have those four teams shown during the early weeks of this season? BBC Sport NI explores some of the talking points from within each club.

For Dungannon Swifts, the most obvious improvement has been the manner in which they have recovered from their opening day defeat.

Rodney McAree's side began the campaign with a 3-1 home loss against Coleraine, but have responded with victories over Portadown, Bangor and Cliftonville.

That represents a significant improvement on last season when the Swifts made a really concerning start to the campaign and lost their opening five league fixtures.

Dungannon have secured a top six finish for the past two seasons and manager Rodney McAree will want to repeat the feat this term.

Midfielder Sean McAllister has already stood out, scoring three goals so far and has been heavily involved when the Swifts push into the final third.

New signings such as Kris Lowe have also impressed with former Portadown boss Niall Currie saying the Swifts side is the "strongest" it has ever been, as they aim to seal another chance at European football.

"I look at Rodney McAree's squad now and, to me, this is the strongest Dungannon squad there has been," Currie said on Sportsound.

"Rodney has gone out and got strength and depth. Some of the players who are not even making the squad at the minute for the Swifts are a lot of players who would certainly have started a few years ago."

After last season's seventh-place finish and resultant play-off involvement, and with the team overflowing with Irish League experience, it is maybe no surprise that Carrick have made a strong start to the campaign.

Paul Heatley continues to be a threat in their attack and certainly does not perform like a player who had to be persuaded out of retirement by manager Stephen Baxter in the summer.

The 39-year-old, who signed a new one-year deal during the summer, has already netted three goals so far with his partnership with Danny Gibson continuing to give the opposition's defence headaches.

During their emphatic 4-0 win over Bangor, they were also denied by the woodwork four times with Seasiders manager Lee Feeney saying that his side "were lucky it was only four" , showing the complete dominance that Carrick enjoyed.

It will be a big next few fixtures for Stephen Baxter's side, who face Linfield, Cliftonville Ballymena United, Larne and Glentoran in September.

After only securing their Premiership status last season through the promotion/relegation play-off and then losing their opening fixture against rivals Cliftonville, early alarm bells may have been starting to sound among Crusaders fans.

They have certainly stopped now, though, with the side showing their grit to earn a 2-1 win over Glentoran at the Oval and extend their winning sequence to three.

Following a dismal 2025-26 campaign, it was a challenging off season for Declan Caddell, who has had to rebuild his team following key player's exits such as Fraser Bryden and Musa Dibaga.

Caddell opted once again to explore the Scottish market during the transfer window and, so far, the new signings have impressed with Scots Owen Wardell and Aaron Reid scoring in east Belfast.

Last season, the Crues struggled due to relying on Bryden for goals but pressing on the counter-attack has emerged as one of the new tactics the side are using early this season.

"They have been good on the counter-attack. When they have done it, they have created opportunities," said Sean Ward after their win over Glentoran.

"Crusaders have relied on hitting on the counter which is a strategy I have no doubt they will use for much of the season.

Few clubs will attract as much attention after an opening day defeat as Linfield did when they lost against Ballymena United, a result that immediately raised questions around how the side would respond.

However, after another professional display from the Blues which saw them breeze past Limavady, they have now won three games in a row and registered clean sheets in their past two matches.

At the Limavady Showgrounds, Adam Frizzell assisted Matthew Fitzptarick's opening goal of the season before scoring himself in the second half.

Questions still remain around the Linfield squad and its depth which will likely be tested as the season progresses, but the side have already shown the qualities needed to bounce back from disappointment.

The experienced David Healy will know more than most that the table will change constantly but he will also be aware that the opening weekends are far from irrelevant as the race for the Gibson Cup starts to heat up.

articles.title: Sam Parkin's EFL takeaways including Charlton's perfect start
articles.summary: BBC Final Score pundit Sam Parkin looks at the weekend's talking points in the EFL, including a perfect start for Charlton Athletic.
articles.body:
With most sides having completed their opening three matches of the new season, BBC Final Score pundit Sam Parkin gives his takeaways from across the EFL on some of the early high flyers and strugglers.

Impressive Charlton won't get carried away

Charlton finished 19th in the Championship in 2025-2026 after coming up from League One the previous season, so does three successive wins suggest the Addicks are ready to 'kick-on'?

Parkin: "I'm sure if you offered Nathan Jones and the most ardent of supporters a mid-table finish now, they'd snap your hand off for it. So, I don't think anyone will be getting carried away.

"I think that first season is always about staying in the division, being defensively strong. The majority of their victories last season were by narrow margins - like today.

"I think they look a bit more attacking this season. He played a wing-back system before, and they they look like they're playing with wingers this season, which is a bit more attack-minded.

"When they got promoted, they signed a lot of good lads from League One to try and make the step up with them to the Championship. This summer I think there's been a slightly different tack there in terms of recruitment, with a lot more experience - like today's goalscorer Karlan Grant and Nathaniel Chalobah - coming to The Valley.

"There's definitely slight differences in the way that they're setting up, and the style".

Charlton maintain 100% start against lowly Preston

Swansea have had three successive mid-table finishes in the Championship, but Saturday's 3-0 win at Derby continued their flying start to 2025-2026 with seven points from three games so far:

Parkin: "Despite the manager (Victor Matos) being there last year, I think they were probably a little bit unknown coming into the season.

"They had a really interesting summer in terms of the players they signed, bringing in Celtic defender Stephen Welsh, and today's first scorer - Ghana winger Joseph Opoku - from Belgium.

"So, I think they're quite forward thinking in the way that they go about signing players, and and the one thing about Swansea is you that, give or take, you know the way they are going to play. It's always quite a stylish brand of football.

"I think they've had a terrific start, but I'm not sure they'll have the consistency to be challenging the higher echelons of the division, but now that the play-offs are extended to six teams, they could look to maybe make one of those positions.

"The other side of the coin is obviously Derby are winless and it was probably a good time to play Derby, with their injuries and the frustrations over the takeover not happening."

Burnley agreed to part company with former Championship-winning manager Scott Parker in the summer, and bring in former Genk boss Nicky Hayen - but they are yet to win in the league:

Parkin: "It's the case with all the relegated sides that you have to give them a little bit of time to acclimatize. I think that's natural. There might be some in the dressing room who don't see themselves as being second-tier footballers.

"That's the reality, and some may still move before the window closes, so we won't know exactly what squad he'll be working with. But my sentiment with them is that they've got brilliant individuals, whoever sticks around, and I'm sure they'll be able to add as well in both the windows.

"So they're going to be competitive in terms of the quality of players. It's just getting that cohesion, which may take a bit of time with a new manager.

"Probably in contrast to West Ham and Wolves who I think have both got real goal power, I'm not sure I'm seeing the same kind of power in that area of the pitch for Burnley.

"There's not a number of them that jump off the page that are going to guarantee a good return of goals. That would be my biggest question mark about them at the moment.

"But as hard as it'll be for supporters to hear, I don't think it's any shame losing at Norwich, because Norwich are going to be right up there in my opinion this season. That's probably a given considering how well they finished last season under Philippe Clement."

The Owls finally saw new ownership take over the club this summer after a long battle, and beat Bromley 7-2 in front of 30,000 fans at Hillsbrough:

Parkin: "Despite the pain of the past few years and the fans' uncertainty, they've got their club to go and support again, and albeit it's in the third tier, the attendances will be huge.

"They never wavered their support really under very, very difficult ownership to put it lightly across the past few years. So there's a new dawn there.

"The side played well against Bradford, certainly for 45 minutes in their maiden home game in the league this season, but just couldn't get the goal.

"So to get those early goals today in the first half will have given them the belief to go on. They've got some really exciting young players and, despite them being in League One, with the size of that club, people want to go and play for you.

"People will want to be on that journey. They'll want to play in front of a packed crowd every week, and the club name will sell itself.

"They're going to be strong. I thought it'd probably take a little bit of time, but that will do them wonders today getting such a handsome victory at home."

Salford owners will be scratching their heads

Salford City finished eighth in 2024-2025, and then lost the 2025-2026 League Two play-of final, before sacking Karl Robinson. His successor, Peter Cklamovski, has lost his opening three league matches:

Parkin: "If you were a fan, you'd have been really enthused again in the transfer window. Two names that jump out at me - Luke Molyneux, probably the best attacking player at Doncaster for a number of seasons, and striker Macaulay Langstaff from Millwall.

"He didn't have a great time at Millwall in terms of goals, but he's probably better than League Two. So to get those two over the line in the summer, naturally, you would have felt that, attacking wise, they were going to be very good - and it's not translated that way in the opening weeks of the season.

"It's early days, but the ownership will be scratching their heads a little bit, because the budget will be very competitive again and beaten play-off finalists last year, you'd expect them to be around it. So, really surprised.

"It'll get better for them, I'm sure, but when you take the Salford job, you're always under probably a bit more pressure than some of the jobs in League Two because of the resources and the magnitude of some of the names that are involved."

Sam Parkin was speaking to BBC Sport England's Tim Durrans

articles.title: Bill Belichick, UNC Beat TCU as CFB Fans React to 2026 Season Opener in Ireland
articles.summary: Bill Belichick and the North Carolina Tar Heels defeated the TCU Horned Frogs 15-10 on Saturday, securing the victory behind a strong defensive performance and scoring effort in preseason action.
articles.body:
Bill Belichick and the North Carolina Tar Heels defeated the TCU Horned Frogs 15-10 on Saturday, securing the victory behind a strong defensive performance and scoring effort in preseason action.

The Horned Frogs were an 8.5-point favorite over the Tar Heels, according to FanDuel Sportsbook , but could not translate their championship-caliber talent to Aviva Stadium in Dublin, Ireland.

Both TCU and North Carolina found field goals and touchdowns in an exciting opening quarter, finishing the period knotted at 10.

UNC's Jaylen McGill rushed for a 9-yard touchdown, scoring the Tar Heels' first touchdown of the season on a 70-yard, seven-play drive down the field.

The Tar Heels' defense stood strong in the second quarter, forcing a turnover on downs to open the period and recording a safety for two points.

The offense then committed a fumble before the close of the half, but TCU could not capitalize, going three-and-out as the Tar Heels took a 12-10 lead into the break.

Maybe the absence of defensive coordinator and Belichick's son, Steve Belichick, was for the best in Ireland, as the Tar Heels looked as impressive as they have since the two joined the program in 2025.

It was announced Aug. 6 that Steve would be out indefinitely on medical leave as the team's defensive coordinator, with the staff set to coach the defense collectively in the meantime, per USA Today's Austin Curtright .

The second half saw UNC's defense force two turnovers on downs and record one forced fumble, adding to the two turnovers on downs and safety it forced in the first half as the Tar Heels cruised to a 15-10 victory.

In Belichick's first year coaching college football, choosing the Tar Heels as his new home, the team finished a disappointing 4-8, including 2-6 in the ACC, under the former six-time Super Bowl-winning head coach and starting quarterback Gio Lopez.

Lopez transferred to the Wake Forest Demon Deacons for his junior season, making way for senior quarterback Edwards Jr., formerly of the Wisconsin Badgers program.

After his subpar opening college football season out east, Belichick placed some of the blame on the dynamic between him and a team he had little part in recruiting.

"The group last year, I mean, I wouldn't say they were, like, disrespectful, that's not the right word, but it was just different," Belichick said on Barstool Sports' Pardon My Take (h/t Sports Illustrated 's Logan Lazarczyk ). "It was like they were recruited by somebody else; they came here for somebody else."

"I was new, they were leaving, you know. It wasn't a bad relationship, but it wasn't a great one," Belichick continued. "There wasn't the same kind of adhesion that there is to guys that you bring in, that come there because of you, because they want to be with you. And then you grow together."

With a promising Week 0 victory in the books, North Carolina is looking to shed the woes of last season as it enters the 2026 regular season against East Tennessee State on Saturday, Sept. 12, seeking a regular season opening win at home.

articles.title: España sigue arrollando en su camino hacia el Mundial Femenino
articles.standfirst: La selección se mantiene invicta tras aplastar a Mali, rival en la fase de grupos, mientras va incorporando a las internacionales que militan en la WNBA
articles.summary: La selección se mantiene invicta tras aplastar a Mali, rival en la fase de grupos, mientras va incorporando a las internacionales que militan en la WNBA
articles.body: Cuatro de cuatro para la selección femenina en su preparación de cara al Mundial que arranca el próximo viernes. En el penúltimo amistoso, España pasó por encima de Mali, que será su segundo rival en la fase de grupos del campeonato. Aplastante triunfo por 97-58 con muy buenas sensaciones, gran intensidad defensiva, mucho acierto desde el triple (16/25) y numerosas jugadoras a alto nivel. Todas anotaron y ninguna llegó a estar 23 minutos en pista. Brillo para la más veterana, Alba Torrens, y para la más joven, Iyana Martín. Ambas lideraron la anotación española con 13 puntos. La primera lució de inicio. La segunda, cuando la selección terminó de romper el partido en el segundo cuarto (45-21). Maite Cazorla (12) y Andrea Vilaró (11) destacaron desde el triple con tres por cabeza y María Araujo fue una navaja suiza: seis puntos, siete rebotes y cinco asistencias. Todas las internacionales se han propuesto ponerle complicado los descartes al seleccionador Miguel Méndez, que aún debe incorporar a las cinco jugadoras que militan en la WNBA. Awa Fam y María Conde ya se han entrenado y podrían tener minutos este domingo en la última prueba ante China (21.00 horas). Megan Gustafson, Raquel Carrera y Alicia Flórez son las últimas en unirse. España marcó territorio desde el inicio con un 10-0 de arranque. A Mali le costaba pasar de medio campo y, cuando no perdía el balón ante la presión española, se le echaba encima el reloj de posesión. Fue la tónica de toda la tarde. Las africanas acumularon 27 pérdidas. Tampoco la selección cuidó bien el balón (19), pero lo compensó con 29 asistencias y, sobre todo, con una intensidad y una concentración que no se cesaron. Las rentas fueron creciendo con el paso de los minutos y, mediado el segundo acto, con Iyana Martín a los mandos, España ya doblaba a su rival: 38-19. Mali no veía aro y al descanso llevaba un pobre 5/19 en tiros de dos puntos. El 50-26 del intermedio convirtió toda la segunda parte en un banco de pruebas para Miguel Méndez. Las últimas, este domingo frente a los muchos centímetros de China, actual subcampeona del Mundo. Después, llegará el momento de dar las 12 que estarán en la cita de Berlín. 97 – España (25+25+25+22): Cazorla (12), Martín (13), Pueyo (7), Araújo (6), Ginzo (7) -quinteto inicial-Buenavida (7), Etxarri (5), Ortiz (6), Torrens (13), Vilaró (11), Pendande (6) y Hermosa (4). 58 – Mali (14+12+19+13): Doumbia (3), Maimouna (2), Ndiaye (10), Dembelé (6), A. Sangare (11) -quinteto inicial-, Sissoko (1), Sanou (-), Sidiki (4), D. Sangare (-), Kamite (15), Balayera (-), Coulibaly (2), Cissé (4). Árbitros: Roberto Lucas (España), Xavi Torres (España), Sandra Sánchez (España). Incidencias: partido amistoso disputado en el Pabellón Príncipe Felipe (Zaragoza).

articles.title: Cody Gakpo: Manchester City open talks with Liverpool about transfer
articles.summary: The Netherlands forward has also attracted interest from Tottenham, but sources indicate Manchester City is his preferred destination if he leaves Anfield.
articles.body:
Manchester City have opened talks with Liverpool about signing attacker Cody Gakpo.

The Netherlands forward's future is set to become one of the key storylines heading into the final three days of the transfer window.

The 27-year-old has attracted concrete interest from City and Tottenham Hotspur , but sources indicate that City is Gakpo's preferred destination if he leaves Anfield before Tuesday's deadline.

City made formal contact with Liverpool over a move on Saturday evening.

Gakpo's potential exit comes after Liverpool agreed to sign Paris St-Germain winger Bradley Barcola in a deal worth up to £123m.

However, it is understood that Liverpool would prefer to sign another forward before sanctioning Gakpo's exit this summer.

The Reds have an interest in Brighton winger Yankuba Minteh and Crystal Palace's Ismaila Sarr .

Gakpo joined Liverpool from boyhood club PSV Eindhoven in January 2023 and has scored 33 goals in 91 Premier League appearances.

On Saturday, he provided the assist for Alexander Isak's goal as Andoni Iraola's side drew 2-2 with Nottingham Forest at Anfield, having scored in last week's draw at Newcastle .

'Liverpool taking massive risk' - analysis

Liverpool view Gakpo as a proven multi-functional Premier League attacker and he has shown that with a goal and an assist in their first two games this season.

But all summer, the understanding has been that if the club bring in the attacking players they want, they would not stand in the way of Gakpo if a solid offer came in.

Given how late in the transfer window the talks are taking place between Liverpool and Manchester City , the Anfield side will now consider the situation before sanctioning any move.

Liverpool are also hoping to bring in another winger before deadline day.

With the arrival of Victor Munoz, the emergence of Rio Ngumoha and Barcola's imminent move from PSG, Gakpo is well aware that he may not be first choice any more, so if a move does happen it would not come as a surprise.

Financially it will be a great outcome for Liverpool if they agree a deal for about £85m given they signed Gakpo for £35m from PSV Eindhoven after the World Cup in 2022.

But with Hugo Ekitike missing until 2027 with a ruptured Achilles tendon, and Isak's injury struggles, they would be taking a massive risk letting Gakpo leave.

articles.title: Matarazzo: "Era muy importante ganar en el primer partido con nuestra afición"
articles.standfirst: El técnico de la Real se mostró muy satisfecho con el rendimiento de sus futbolistas, tras la victoria lograda ante el Espanyol en el estreno oficial en este curso en Anoeta
articles.summary: El técnico de la Real se mostró muy satisfecho con el rendimiento de sus futbolistas, tras la victoria lograda ante el Espanyol en el estreno oficial en este curso en Anoeta
articles.body: Pellegrino Matarazzo se mostró muy satisfecho con el triunfo de su Real Sociedad ante el Espanyol, porque llegó después de una buena actuación de sus futbolistas, encabezados por un gran Mikel Oyarzabal. Matarazzo compareció ante los medios de comunicación satisfecho por el triunfo. “Ha sido muy importante la victoria de hoy, porque era el primer partido en casa, con nuestra afición, era la primera oportunidad para conectar con los seguidores y, aunque hemos tenido algunas dificultades, conseguimos el triunfo y creo que el rendimiento del equipo ha sido muy bueno. Habíamos hablado antes del partido de que era importante volver a ganar y estoy contento por ello”. El técnico realista dio su versión sobre la tarjeta roja. “En el momento estaba sorprendido, porque no entendía porque que me había sacado la tarjeta roja. Es una situación nueva, cuando el portero estaba siendo atendido y hay que sacar un futbolista fuera. Estábamos decidiendo y él ha sacado a Zubeldia fuera, era un momento complicado y emocionante. Podía habernos avisado que había mucha gente protestando en el área técnica o incluso sacarme amarilla, pero me sacó la roja y creo que es un gran castigo, insisto que se trata de una situación nueva”.

articles.title: Manolo González: "Que los dos goles lleguen al contraataque me asquea bastante”
articles.standfirst: El técnico perico se mostraba enfadado tras el mal partido de lo suyos y era crítico con los goles encajados
articles.summary: El técnico perico se mostraba enfadado tras el mal partido de lo suyos y era crítico con los goles encajados
articles.body: El Espanyol cayó ante la Real Sociedad y la imagen que mostró el equipo perico estuvo lejos de la deseada. Los errores atrás y en salida de balón lastraron a un Espanyol que ha mostrado mordiente en ataque pero que cometió mucho errores. Manolo González comparecía en rueda de prensa tras el partido y se mostraba enfadado tras la derrota y ha sido crítico con la imagen del equipo y con los dos tantos encajados. También ha criticado la actitud de los futbolistas en los duelos y ha hablado sobre el cambio al descanso de Urko González. Valoración del partido: "Con la jugada del 1-0, que te penaliza mucho, ya empiezas en el minuto cuatro a remolque. A partir de ahí el partido ya se complica y vuelve a ser lo mismo. Hemos hablado mucho durante la semana del tema vigilancias, de la situación de Oyarzabal, la colocación a la espalda de los medios, que por eso ha entrado Moscardo en la segunda parte también, que pienso que lo ha hecho bien. Han sido muchas pérdidas de balón, con situaciones que no tenían presión y perdíamos la pelota fácil, pienso que en la segunda parte, cuando mejor estábamos, el equipo tenía el partido más controlado y estábamos llegando, es cuando ha llegado la situación del 2-1. Ahí se ha complicado otra vez. Hoy pienso que el partido no es bueno, está claro, pero no es bueno sobre todo porque los jugadores no han estado bien, a nivel general no han estado bien y a nivel individual tampoco". Crítico con las pérdidas de balón: "Cuando vienes aquí puedes pensar que el rival te puede sorprender a través del juego o de la posesión. No ha sido así y las situaciones de peligro las hemos provocado nosotros con pérdidas, sin tener una presión excesiva del rival y con situaciones de defender mal las vigilancias. Hoy hemos estado mal y hemos concedido muchas situaciones de contras, que me fastidia bastante, la verdad. A mí lo que me molesta mucho de hoy es que nos hayan metido dos goles de contraataque. A mí eso sí que me fastidia bastante". Falta de contundencia en los duelos: "La Real ha matado y el Espanyol no ha sido capaz de hacerlo cuando ha tenido la posibilidad. Han sido situaciones bastante claras, sobre todo la de Javi dentro del área. Cuando ha comenzado la segunda parte hemos estado estables porque no ha habido pérdidas tontas como en la primera y porque las vigilancias estaban bien. El momento que nos hemos equivocado con la vigilancia ha venido el 2-1 y lo que decíamos, te dejan 3-4 jugadores descolgados, que cuando atacas m lo tienes que ajustar bien. Hemos tenido pérdidas que no nos podemos permitir en Primera División. A nivel de duelos ha ido Roberto, Marcos cuando ha salido ha estado bien a nivel de duelos, pero lo que no puede ser es que más de la mitad del equipo no gane en duelos individuales. Moscardo cuando ha entrado ha estado bien". Sobre el cambio de Urko: "El otro día sí que hice muchos cambios por amarillas, hoy ha sido un cambio porque no estaba bien. Yo ayer hablé de Urko en rueda de prensa y hablé muy bien, pues mira, a veces es mejor no hablar, porque hoy no ha estado bien. Hoy hay que decirlo, Urko es un jugador importante para nosotros, que ha demostrado un gran nivel con nosotros, pero hoy no ha estado bien, ni en duelos ni con balón y encima con amarilla, pues el cambio creo que era bastante obvio". Sobre las amonestaciones al final del encuentro: "Es lo que decimos de la regla, que al final todo el mundo intentará jugar con esto. Al final lo que ha pasado es que hemos estado parados. Cuando haces una cosa de estas, ya sabes que la trampa vendrá detrás. Al final han pasado dos minutos desde la jugada de córner hasta que se ha lanzado y en este aspecto sí que es mejorable”.

articles.title: Oficial: Héctor Fort firma hasta 2031
articles.standfirst: El defensa catalán se convierte en el segundo fichaje para este curso 2026-27 de una Real que paga al Barcelona unos 8,5 millones de euros por el 60% de su derechos
articles.summary: El defensa catalán se convierte en el segundo fichaje para este curso 2026-27 de una Real que paga al Barcelona unos 8,5 millones de euros por el 60% de su derechos
articles.body: La Real Sociedad ha hecho oficial una hora después del triunfo ante el Espanyol el fichaje de Héctor Fort hasta 2031 procedente del Fútbol Club Barcelona, al que el club txuriurdin, que en esta ocasión no ha ofrecido los datos, pagaría 8,5 millones de euros por el 60% de sus derechos, teniendo los culés una opción de compra de unos 20 millones. Fort, que ha visto desde un palco de Anoeta el triunfo de su nuevo equipo ante el Espanyol por 2-1, se convierte así en al segunda incorporación de la Real para la temporada 2026-27, tras la de Mamadou Sarr. El conjunto txuriurdin fue el más goleado del pasado campeonato y tras el entendió que debía mejorar su defensa, por lo que se ha hecho con un central y un lateral derecho. En el caso del segundo puesto, los técnicos realistas decidieron hace unas semanas bajar a Iñaki Rupérez al Sanse y salir al mercado para buscar la contratación de Fort, que parecía cerca del Borussia Dortmund, pero al que lograron finalmente convencer para recalar en San Sebastián, a la vez que al Barcelona para acceder al acuerdo. El segundo fichaje de la Real para la 2026-27 realizará este domingo su primer entrenamiento a las órdenes de Pellegrino Matarazzo y con sus nuevos compañeros, estando probablemente en disposición de entrar en la convocatoria para recibir al Celta el próximo jueves, encuentro en el que podría debutar como txuriurdin. Héctor Fort se formó en las categorías inferiores del Barcelona. Debutó con el primer equipo azulgrana en la temporada 2023/24, en un partido de Champions frente al Royal Antwerp en el que salió de titular. La campaña siguiente jugó con el primer equipo, disputando 20 partidos con Hansi Flick en el banquillo. Las cosas cambiaron la temporada anterior, porque ya no estuvo en el Barcelona y se fue cedido junto a Iñaki Peña al Elche. Aunque Fort quería convencer al entrenador alemán durante esta pretemporada, finalmente no ha sido así y el club lo ha vendido a la Real Sociedad.

articles.title: Newcastle duo Anthony Elanga and Yoane Wissa thriving under Matthias Jaissle after win over Tottenham - Premier League hits and misses
articles.summary: Sky Sports football writers analyse Saturday's action as Anthony Elanga and Yoane Wissa form the heartbeat of Matthias Jaissle's positive start at Newcastle; Rayan Cherki stars in Man City win over Palace; Hull City fly the flag for the Premier League newcomers
articles.body:
"In Elanga and Wissa, it's like two new players!" said Sky Sports' Jamie Carragher as Newcastle picked up their first win by beating Tottenham.

Anthony Elanga netted his second goal of the season after shining in their 2-2 draw against Liverpool while Yoane Wissa grabbed his first as the rejuvenated pair continued to show their quality at last.

Newcastle head coach Matthias Jaissle is doing what Eddie Howe couldn't with the duo that were signed for £110m last summer. He also handed midfielder Nico Gonzalez a debut and it was his pass that led to Elanga's opener.

For all the talk of a season of struggle under their new boss after another difficult transfer window, their supporters left the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium singing about Europe.

Their chants may have been tongue in cheek, but they will be buoyed by Jaissle's fresh approach, with a side playing with the freedom and togetherness to challenge for European places. David Richardson

In case it wasn't clear, Rayan Cherki is Manchester City's talisman. Erling Haaland is there to get the goals, and as he did at Selhurst Park, will rarely leave margin for error in front of goal.

But as City cry out for a difference-maker between the boxes, Cherki is the one who stands tallest in response.

With two goals and two assists already this campaign, there's a new look to Manchester City's No 10 who showed flashes of his brilliance last season. He decided the game at Selhurst Park, first with a neat slalom through Palace's defence and the second with an audacious strike on his weak foot from range.

So many thought that Kevin De Bruyne's passing of the guard was to Phil Foden. However, under the sheer audacity of Cherki's approach to the game, Foden's role is that of a supporting act.

At the PFA awards this week, Bruno Fernandes alluded to the fact that Cherki could be the player to take his assist record that he claimed just three months ago.

By the looks of things, the way Cherki has started, he could be on the hunt for more than just Fernandes' assist crown. William Bitibiri

Cody Gakpo has attracted interest from Tottenham and Manchester City and with Deadline Day fast approaching his future is far from certain. The impending arrival of Bradley Barcola has also fuelled talk that the Dutchman will be heading for the exit.

But at the same time, Gakpo has been one of Liverpool's best performers during their stuttering start to the season. He scored at Newcastle last weekend and could have had more. On Saturday he put Isak's goal on a plate with a sumptuous cross after getting in down the right.

The switch of flanks from his favoured left side didn't deter him and he was Liverpool's brightest spark during the first half when they otherwise struggled. That versatility is a trait which is important to Iraola with the way he likes his wingers to operate.

This early-season good form from Gakpo, though, could soon be continued in a different club's shirt, should Liverpool receive an offer and opt to cash-in before 11pm on Tuesday. His impactful performances could convince his admirers to make their bid. Peter Smith

Alex Scott is an outstanding talent. The 23-year-old impressed again against Everton on Saturday and is now the beating heart of this Bournemouth team.

Despite an early booking for a late challenge, Scott controlled the midfield with extreme confidence and his goal just before half-time was thoroughly deserved. It was the perfect example of how he plays the game - composure under pressure and effortless precision.

But there was much more to his performance than just that. Against the Toffees, Scott had more touches than any other player (85), made the most defensive contributions (15), covered 11km and completed 11 passes into the final third. He contributed at both ends of the pitch.

Before the game, Bournemouth boss Marco Rose was "120 per cent" confident that Scott would stay beyond Deadline Day despite interest from Manchester City and Chelsea. With two years remaining on his contract, the Cherries insist he is not for sale and there is no reason to suggest he won't be at the club this time next week.

But if Scott keeps putting in performances like this one, it surely won't be long before the big boys start knocking firmly on the door. For Bournemouth's sake, let's hope they can enjoy him for a while longer yet. Dan Sansom

Everyone was excited about Coventry's return to the Premier League. After all, they were the Championship winners and arrived back in the top flight with plenty of optimism.

Two games in, though, it is Hull who are flying the flag for the promoted sides.

The Tigers scraped into the play-offs on the final day before edging their way up - and now they have beaten Manchester United and Coventry to sit second with six points from six.

There was something seriously impressive about this one. Hull were happy to let Coventry have the ball, soak up the pressure and wait for their moment - and when it came, Liam Millar delivered.

Oli McBurnie's point that these are the games that really matter could prove crucial come May.

Jakirovic, meanwhile, is having none of the early title talk despite chants from fans. Wise man.

But with two wins from two, Hull are certainly giving everyone something to talk about. William Bitibiri

articles.title: William Jewell announces death of RB MicahJo Barnett after medical emergency on sideline
articles.summary: The game between William Jewell and Fort Lewis was suspended after the first quarter after Barnett reportedly suffered 'seizure-like symptoms.'
articles.body:
William Jewell announced that junior running back MicahJo Barnett has died. Barnett appeared to suffer a medical emergency on the sideline during the Cardinals' home opener against Fort Lewis on Saturday.

"William Jewell College and the Liberty, Missouri community mourn the passing of Micah Jo Barnett," the school wrote in a statement . "Our thoughts and prayers are with Micah Jo's family, our students, the Cardinal Football family, and the rest of our community during this time of loss."

Per the school, a vigil to honor Barnett will be held Saturday night.

Play was suspended in the first quarter on Saturday after Barnett began suffering from what Liberty Fire EMS called "seizure-like symptoms," via Fox4 KC's Harold R. Kuntz . The game was later called off, with Kuntz reporting that Jewell players were emotional as they left the facility.

Barnett, a junior, was majoring in business administration, per the athletic department's website . He was born in Shawnee, KS and attended Liberty North High School, winning a Missouri state championship his senior year.

After playing in eight games as a freshman at William Jewell, Barnett started in five games last season before suffering a season-ending injury. Barnett also received all-Great Lakes Valley Conference academic honors last season.
